llm.summary: This skill is mostly a code-quality helper, but it asks agents to bypass stopping limits and includes an external posting workflow that needs careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Repo scanning and targeted refactoring are proportionate for code refinement, but unbounded execution waves and external publication of code findings are broader than the main description discloses.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No executable install script was present in the artifact; the metadata identifies it as a port from claude-night-market/pensive with optional cross-plugin configuration dependencies.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact explicitly allows phrases like "ignore scope guard" and instructs agents to continue past branch-size limits, avoid mid-task checkpoints, and resume after a harness stop signal.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no daemon or startup persistence, but the runtime instructions create operational persistence by telling the agent to keep executing, record closure commits, update docs, and resume after stop signals.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core code-quality analysis is purpose-aligned, and default invocation is plan-only, but the skill also defines execution modes that can apply broad repository changes and a module that posts findings to GitHub Discussions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a skill that can go beyond analysis into repository-wide refactoring. Prefer plan-only use, require explicit approval before any edits or commits, do not use scope-override phrasing, and disable or review the insight-generation module before allowing findings to be posted externally.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Code modification can fit a skill described as improving code quality, and the artifact says no-qualifier invocation is plan-only, so the general analysis-versus-editing concern is only partly supported.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The execution section is disclosed but materially overbroad: it can run all waves to closure, require commit-based closure records, and proceed without clear per-wave approval.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The stop-boundary concern is supported by artifact text allowing branch-size override and instructing immediate resumption after a harness stop signal.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The insight module directs refinement findings, including concrete code evidence, to GitHub Discussions after analysis, which is not part of the main skill description.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The insight module includes a concrete command that changes into a fixed local path and invokes a posting script, creating an outbound data flow without an explicit user approval gate.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad triggers such as refactoring and duplication are normal for a code-quality skill, but they increase risk because the same skill also contains write-capable execution paths.
[SSD-1] unexpected: The natural-language phrase "ignore scope guard" is accepted as an execution control override, which is not necessary for code refinement.
[SSD-4] unexpected: The completion-gate language discourages normal checkpoints and asks the agent to keep working until every candidate is closed or rationalized.
